### Stack plan

- One branch and one PR per reviewable change. Every PR of one delivery stacks in work order by default, so each is reviewed and merged atop the one before it; the target repository's own conventions come first, and where they ask for independent PRs, set the state mode as Version control says. Every new PR, a delivery's first included, starts from the open stack's top: the owner's non-draft PRs (never forks or others' PRs, whose branches the root cannot push to), the one it depends on, else the most recently updated; it starts from the base only when it adds CI, no stack is open, or conventions ask for independent PRs.
- When the work adds CI, its PR comes first, from the base, so every later PR runs it.
- Parallel writers get disjoint paths, shared types and files included; overlap costs conflicts and a second review.
- Verify real PR bases rather than inferring them from names. No aggregate PR.
- Each PR targets the branch its writer starts from: for a delivery's first PR, the open stack's top or the base, as the first bullet sets, else its immediate predecessor. When lower PRs change, merge forward with merge commits, once per batch of repairs, and push the affected branches together. Before stacking on a lagging open stack, merge the base into its lowest branch, then forward up the stack. Published history is never rewritten or force-pushed; a rewrite goes to the user. A merge made outside review (a merge-forward, a conflict resolution, a merge from the base) gets a review of that head before any push. Rebuild a conflicted generated file with the project's build task.
- Commit the writer's work locally first and review that commit; repairs are new local commits. Push only after the reviews accept, and in the same step open each pushed branch's PR ready for review (or update it with `vcs pr --update <n>`), so nothing stays only local or unlisted. Each PR's head passes the gates alone, and the next PR stacks on one once the independent review accepts it, not human review.
- Branch names follow the repository's convention. Without one and when the version workflow fits, use `release/<version>/<type>/<change>` for release work and `exp/<experiment>/<type>/<change>` for experiments, keeping the project's real version string. A name grants no merge, release or deploy authority.
